title: Numbers and BigInt (appropriate use)
learningObjectives: Explain numbers and bigint (appropriate use) and write predictable JavaScript code using the concept.

understand.concept: JavaScript's Number type uses IEEE 754 double-precision floating-point values. It supports integers and decimals within its precision limits. BigInt represents integers of arbitrary size within implementation limits and is written with an n suffix. BigInt and Number cannot be mixed directly in arithmetic.
understand.whyItMatters: Floating-point arithmetic can produce rounding effects, and Number cannot represent every large integer exactly. Choose BigInt for large integer calculations when appropriate, and use decimal-safe approaches for money.
understand.analogy: Number is a flexible measuring scale with finite precision; BigInt is an integer type for values that exceed the safe integer range.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript values, scope, and runtime behaviour follow the language specification.

explain.narrative: The calculation uses Number for a small decimal amount and BigInt for a large integer. Real financial calculations should use an appropriate decimal or integer-minor-unit strategy.

examples.explanation: The calculation uses Number for a small decimal amount and BigInt for a large integer. Real financial calculations should use an appropriate decimal or integer-minor-unit strategy.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser page or developer console shows the values and behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Compare Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER with a larger integer. Try adding a BigInt and a Number and explain why explicit conversion is required.
practise.independentTask: Write a short program that uses the concept in a realistic learning-app example. Inspect values and errors in the console.
hints: Prefer const unless reassignment is required.
Do not expose private data in console output.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Numbers and BigInt (appropriate use)</title></head><body>
<script>const price=19.99;const quantity=3;const total=price*quantity;const huge=9007199254740993n;console.log(total,Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER,huge);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which suffix marks a BigInt literal?
questions.explanation: BigInt integer literals use the n suffix.

questions.prompt: What should a learner do when a JavaScript value behaves unexpectedly?
